subject: Game Theory
title: Alliance Formation
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Alliance Formation.

hook.text: NATO started with 12 members in 1949. Today it has 31. Why do nations form military alliances?

buildup.text: Alliances are commitment devices: an attack on one triggers a response from all, raising the cost of aggression.

discovery.text: Burden-sharing is the alliance's dilemma: each member wants others to spend more on defense.

twist.text: The US pays a disproportionate share of NATO's costs. Smaller members free-ride on American protection.

climax.text: Alliances work when the commitment is credible. Would the US really risk war to defend a small ally?

punchline.text: Alliances deter when doubt is minimal.

quiz.question: What is the free-rider problem in alliances?
options: Smaller members rely on larger ones to bear defense costs
